extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: An elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples are roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline, followed by human review to ensure visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and requirement of advanced multi-modal capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples were collected from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: two focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Samples were effectively transformed from uni-modal to multi-modal formats to prevent LLMs from recalling the correct answers, and all questions were ensured to be converted into a multiple-choice format.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated pipeline was used to preliminarily filter out samples lacking visual dependency or having data leakage. Eight LLMs were used as inspectors, and only samples with two or fewer correct hits by these LLMs were retained.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted a manual review process to ensure each sample's answer is based on visual content understanding, covers comprehensive capability dimensions, and requires advanced multi-modal abilities.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To expedite manual selection and ensure diversity in difficulty, the hit counts of 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples were tallied to split them into four difficulty categories (easy, moderate, hard, tough) before final manual curation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, and other LLMs/LVLMs
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand the benchmark into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain visual dependency and reduce data leakage.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current dataset is static, which may eventually lead to accidental data leakage into future training corpora.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluating the multi-modal capacities, actual performance gain, and data leakage of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs).

rai:dataCollection.evidence: These samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline, human review is then involved to ensure each curated sample exhibits visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and requires advanced multi-modal capabilities.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: These samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We first choose two benchmarks [27, 21] focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge [51, 30, 20, 29] for our sample collection.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we develop an automated pipeline to preliminarily filter out samples that do not meet the first two criteria. Specifically, we employ two closed-source LLMs... and six open-source LLMs... to serve as inspectors... we only retain those samples with hit counts of two or fewer hits

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: we further employ three experts to conduct the manual review process to ensure: 1) each sample’s answer should be based on the understanding of visual content; 2) selected samples should cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples should require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: To expedite the manual selection of samples with varying difficulty levels for LVLMs, we tally the hit counts of all 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples and split them into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3).

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we use eight powerful LLMs as candidates inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage, including two closed-source APIs (GPT4-Turbo [34], and GeminiPro [41]) and six leading open-source models (e.g., LLaMA-70B [43], Qwen-1.5-72B [1], and Mixtral-8x7B [19]).

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: In the future, we plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM’s and LVLM’s training corpora.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: In the future, we plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM’s and LVLM’s training corpora.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: aiming to evaluate LVLMs’ multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples... Moreover, two metrics are developed to measure data leakage and actual performance gain in multi-modal training.
